history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration make a distinction between operational guidance, to be applied using professional judgment and expertise, and mandatory policies, and issue procurement guidance and policy accordingly.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board. On the basis of the continuous improvements made since 2019 to the instrument relating to delegation of authority from a head of entity for procurement (annex A, updated in November 2023), the revised procurement manual (updated in January 2024) and the various guidelines relating to supply chain operations issued by the Department of Operational Support since 2020 (e.g., on procurement through cooperation with United Nations entities), the Administration deems that the recommendation has been implemented. The Administration appreciates the recommendation and took it fully into account while implementing the improvements mentioned, and each document was the result of close consultation between the Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance and the Department of Operational Support, based on the Departments’ roles as highlighted in the audit findings. Together with the fundamental parameters of procurement set out in the Financial Regulations and Rules of the United Nations (financial regulations 5.12 and 5.13 on general principles), the Administration considers that the current framework is clear to United Nations practitioners and oversight bodies, as demonstrated by the lack of subsequent related audit findings. Upon request, the Administration has, since the issuance of the recommendation, sent several memos and emails to confirm that procurement practitioners are kept fully informed of the applicable enhanced information framework, and therefore would appreciate the Board’s consideration of the new update provided, in order to close the recommendation.
history.board_assessment: The Board notes the progress made in the clarification between mandatory and operational guidance, especially in the most recent version of the procurement manual (June 2024). The updated guidance was disseminated through internal communication. The Board will continue to audit the implementation of the new guidance, especially the updated procurement manual, but considers the recommendation to be implemented.
